---
title: "plot_slopes"
format: html
---

A geographic map of slope values.
This expects the parameterRateOfChange `.csv` files generated by the parameterRateOfChange quartobatch to be in `data/exports/parameterRateOfChange/`.
The latest version of these files produced by that workflow can be downloaded from [this gdrive folder](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1paXYRvTTS1qo2zv5durS0jMRxMCu9kus?usp=drive_link).


## load data
```{R, load data}
library(here)
library(glue)
library(tidyverse)
# parameter_to_plot <- "Nitrate (NO3)"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Phosphate, Filtered (PO4)"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Total Phosphorus"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Total Nitrogen"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Chlorophyll a, Corrected for Pheophytin"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Turbidity"
# parameter_to_plot <- "Water Temperature"
parameter_to_plot <- "Light Extinction Coefficient"
df <- read.csv(here(glue("data/exports/parameterRateOfChange/{parameter_to_plot}.csv")))
```


## exclude data points on land
```{R}
library(sf)
library(maps)

# 1. Filter out rows with missing coordinates to prevent spatial conversion errors
df_valid <- df[!is.na(df$OriginalLongitude) & !is.na(df$OriginalLatitude), ]

# 2. Convert the dataframe into a spatial sf object
df_sf <- st_as_sf(df_valid, coords = c("OriginalLongitude", "OriginalLatitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# 3. Retrieve the Florida land boundary polygon
# (Since SEACAR projects focus on Florida coastal waters, we check against the Florida state boundary)
fl_map <- maps::map("state", region = "florida", fill = TRUE, plot = FALSE)
fl_sf <- st_as_sf(fl_map) %>% st_transform(crs = 4326)

# 4. Check for intersection between the coordinate points and the land polygon
on_land <- st_intersects(df_sf, fl_sf, sparse = FALSE)

# 5. Retain only points that do NOT fall on the land polygon
df_clean <- df_valid[!rowSums(on_land) > 0, ]

message(paste("Removed", nrow(df) - nrow(df_clean), "points located on land."))

# Override the main dataset with the marine-only dataset
df <- df_clean
```


## filter out data points outside the FKNMS boundaries
```{R}
library(sf)

# 1. Filter out missing coordinates
df_valid <- df[!is.na(df$OriginalLongitude) & !is.na(df$OriginalLatitude), ]
df_sf <- st_as_sf(df_valid, coords = c("OriginalLongitude", "OriginalLatitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# 2. Load the local FKNMS boundary shapefile from the zip archive
# We check both the project-relative 'data/' directory and absolute '/data' system path
zip_path <- here("data/fknms_py2.zip")
if (!file.exists(zip_path)) {
  zip_path <- "/data/fknms_py2.zip"
}

fknms_boundary <- tryCatch({
  message(paste("Attempting to load local FKNMS shapefile from:", zip_path))
  
  # Unzip to a temporary directory to extract and read the .shp file cleanly
  temp_dir <- tempfile()
  unzip(zip_path, exdir = temp_dir)
  shp_file <- list.files(temp_dir, pattern = "\\.shp$", full.names = TRUE)
  
  if (length(shp_file) == 0) {
    stop("No .shp file found inside the zip archive.")
  }
  
  st_read(shp_file[1], quiet = TRUE)
}, error = function(e) {
  message(paste("Warning: Failed to load local shapefile (", e$message, "). Falling back to bounding coordinates.", sep = ""))
  # FKNMS extent fallback: West -83.15, East -80.0667, North 25.65, South 24.3
  bbox <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -83.15, ymin = 24.3, xmax = -80.0667, ymax = 25.65), crs = st_crs(4326))
  st_as_sfc(bbox)
})

# Ensure the boundary CRS matches EPSG:4326
fknms_boundary <- st_transform(fknms_boundary, crs = 4326)

# 3. Represent Biscayne Bay as a simple latitudinal/longitudinal bounding box
# Bounded on the north by exactly 26.0°N, and on the west to isolate the Atlantic side
biscayne_bbox <- st_bbox(c(xmin = -80.4, ymin = 25.25, xmax = -80.0, ymax = 26.0), crs = st_crs(4326))
biscayne_boundary <- st_as_sfc(biscayne_bbox)

# 4. Merge the FKNMS and Biscayne Bay boundaries into a single study area
fknms_geom <- st_geometry(fknms_boundary)
study_boundary <- st_union(fknms_geom, biscayne_boundary)

# 5. Check for intersection between points and the combined sanctuary/bay polygon
inside_study_area <- st_intersects(df_sf, study_boundary, sparse = FALSE)

# 6. Filter dataset
df_filtered <- df_valid[rowSums(inside_study_area) > 0, ]

message(paste("Removed", nrow(df) - nrow(df_filtered), "points located outside the FKNMS & Biscayne Bay study area."))

# Override the global dataset with the filtered FKNMS + Biscayne Bay data
df <- df_filtered
```


## load helper functions and common packages
```{R}
library(dplyr)
library(sf)
library(h3jsr)

# Updated helper function to accept a target column variable to aggregate
make_hex_layer <- function(df, res, var_name = "significant_slope") {
  agg <- df |>
    mutate(h3 = point_to_cell(
      cbind(OriginalLongitude, OriginalLatitude),
      res = res
    )) |>
    group_by(h3) |>
    # Dynamically average the column specified in var_name
    summarise(avg_value = mean(.data[[var_name]], na.rm = TRUE),
              n         = n(), .groups = "drop")
  polys <- cell_to_polygon(agg$h3)
  st_sf(agg, geometry = polys, crs = 4326)
}

# Define highlighting bounding boxes for sub-regions (FKNMS breakdown + Biscayne Bay)
regions_list <- list(
  "Biscayne Bay" = st_bbox(c(xmin = -80.40, ymin = 25.35, xmax = -80.00, ymax = 26.0), crs = st_crs(4326)),
  "Upper Keys"   = st_bbox(c(xmin = -80.65, ymin = 24.8, xmax = -80.10, ymax = 25.35), crs = st_crs(4326)),
  "Middle Keys"  = st_bbox(c(xmin = -81.20, ymin = 24.55, xmax = -80.65, ymax = 25.0), crs = st_crs(4326)),
  "Lower Keys"   = st_bbox(c(xmin = -81.95, ymin = 24.40, xmax = -81.20, ymax = 24.90), crs = st_crs(4326)),
  "Marquesas + Dry Tortugas" = st_bbox(c(xmin = -83.15, ymin = 24.30, xmax = -81.95, ymax = 24.80), crs = st_crs(4326))
)

regions_sf <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(regions_list), function(name) {
  st_sf(Region = name, geometry = st_as_sfc(regions_list[[name]]))
}))

regions_sf$Region <- factor(regions_sf$Region, levels = names(regions_list))
```


## create static hexagon map with coordinates
```{R}
library(ggplot2)
library(ggspatial)
library(sf)
library(rnaturalearth)
library(rnaturalearthdata)

# === SET THE VARIABLE YOU WANT TO MAP ===
# Options: "significant_slope", "coefficient.of.variation", or "mean"
target_variable <- "mean" 

# Automatically match case-insensitive options for mean columns
if (!(target_variable %in% names(df))) {
  if ("mean" %in% names(df)) {
    target_variable <- "mean"
  }
}

# Filter for finite values of our chosen variable
df_static <- df %>% filter(is.finite(.data[[target_variable]]))

# 1. Aggregate points into static H3 hexagons
static_res <- 6
hexsf_static <- make_hex_layer(df_static, res = static_res, var_name = target_variable)

# 2. Extract valid non-NA values to calculate scale bounds
valid_vals <- hexsf_static$avg_value[is.finite(hexsf_static$avg_value)]

# 3. Retrieve high-resolution vector land boundaries using rnaturalearth (1:50m medium-scale resolution)
# This includes detailed state lines and neighboring countries/islands (Cuba, Bahamas)
land_states_sf <- ne_states(country = "united states of america", returnclass = "sf") %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

land_world_sf <- ne_countries(scale = "medium", returnclass = "sf") %>% 
  st_transform(crs = 4326)

# 4. Build map layers using high-resolution spatial boundaries
p <- ggplot() +
  # Draw detailed landmass boundaries in dark grey with no city/highway labels
  geom_sf(data = land_world_sf, fill = "#333333", color = "#222222", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = land_states_sf, fill = "#333333", color = "#222222", linewidth = 0.1) +
  # Render the H3 Hexagons using geom_sf
  geom_sf(data = hexsf_static, aes(fill = avg_value), color = "#ffffff", linewidth = 0.2, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Render the regional highlight boxes as colored dashed rectangles
  geom_sf(data = regions_sf, aes(color = Region), fill = NA, linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed") +
  # # Label the regions directly on the map for instant visual recognition
  # geom_sf_label(data = regions_sf, aes(label = Region, color = Region), 
  #               alpha = 0.85, size = 3, fontface = "bold", show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Apply distinct color coding to the highlighted study areas
  scale_color_manual(values = c(
    "Biscayne Bay" = "#E69F00",  # Ochre/Yellow
    "Upper Keys"   = "#56B4E9",  # Sky Blue
    "Middle Keys"  = "#009E73",  # Bluish Green
    "Lower Keys"   = "#CC79A7",   # Reddish Purple
    "Marquesas + Dry Tortugas" = "#D55E00"   # Vermillion/Orange-Red
  ), name = "Regions")

# 5. Apply scale options dynamically based on the target variable
if (target_variable %in% c("Mean", "mean")) {
  # LOG SCALE scale options for positive-only physical concentration values
  # Filter out any non-positive values to prevent log transformations of <= 0
  positive_vals <- valid_vals[valid_vals > 0]
  color_limits <- c(min(positive_vals, na.rm = TRUE), max(positive_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
  
  p <- p + scale_fill_viridis_c(
    trans = "log10",                  
    limits = color_limits,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = paste("Avg", target_variable, "\n(Log10 Scale)")
  )
} else if (target_variable == "significant_slope") {
  # Symmetric bounds and diverging palette for trends/slopes
  quantile_bound <- max(abs(c(
    quantile(valid_vals, 0.25, na.rm = TRUE), 
    quantile(valid_vals, 0.75, na.rm = TRUE)
  )))
  color_limits <- c(-quantile_bound, quantile_bound)
  
  p <- p + scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "BrBG", 
    limits = color_limits,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Avg Significant\nSlope"
  )
} else {
  # Sequential limits and palette for positive-only variance metrics (CV)
  color_limits <- c(0, max(valid_vals, na.rm = TRUE))
  
  p <- p + scale_fill_distiller(
    palette = "YlOrRd", 
    limits = color_limits,
    oob = scales::squish,
    name = "Avg Coefficient\nof Variation"
  )
}

# 6. Add spatial context and render the final plot with a white background panel
p +
  annotation_scale(location = "br", width_hint = 0.5) +
  coord_sf(crs = 4326,
           xlim = range(df_static$OriginalLongitude, na.rm = TRUE) + c(-0.2, 0.2),
           ylim = range(df_static$OriginalLatitude, na.rm = TRUE) + c(-0.2, 0.6)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#f0f0f0", linewidth = 0.2),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  ) +
  # labs(title = paste(gsub("\\.", " ", target_variable), "in", parameter_to_plot),
  #      x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")


```


## create boxplots of data distributions by region
```{R}
library(ggplot2)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)

# 1. Convert the filtered dataset 'df' to an sf spatial object
df_sf_filtered <- st_as_sf(df, coords = c("OriginalLongitude", "OriginalLatitude"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

# 2. Perform a spatial join (left join) to assign each data point to its intersecting bounding box
df_with_regions <- st_join(df_sf_filtered, regions_sf, join = st_intersects)

# 3. Clean and convert back to a standard dataframe
df_plot_box <- df_with_regions %>%
  filter(!is.na(Region)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry()

# 4. Match the active variable configured in the static map chunk
boxplot_variable <- target_variable 

# Filter for finite values of the active target variable
df_plot_box <- df_plot_box %>% filter(is.finite(.data[[boxplot_variable]]))

# 5. Generate the boxplot visualization matching the map region colors
bp <- ggplot(df_plot_box, aes(x = Region, y = .data[[boxplot_variable]], fill = Region)) +
  geom_boxplot(outlier.alpha = 0.3, outlier.size = 1.2, width = 0.5, color = "#222222", notch = TRUE) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(
    "Biscayne Bay"             = "#E69F00",  # Ochre/Yellow
    "Upper Keys"               = "#56B4E9",  # Sky Blue
    "Middle Keys"              = "#009E73",  # Bluish Green
    "Lower Keys"               = "#CC79A7",  # Reddish Purple
    "Marquesas + Dry Tortugas" = "#D55E00"   # Vermillion/Orange-Red
  )) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", color = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_line(color = "#f0f0f0", linewidth = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 15, hjust = 1, face = "bold", color = "#333333"),
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black", linewidth = 0.6)
  ) 
  # scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.01, 0.01)) 
  # labs(
  #   title = paste("Parameter: ", parameter_to_plot, " | Total points: ", nrow(df_plot_box), sep=""),
  #   x = "Region",
  #   y = gsub("\\.", " ", boxplot_variable)
  # )

# 6. Apply logarithmic y-scaling if mapping Mean values for scale consistency
if (boxplot_variable %in% c("mean")) {
  bp <- bp + scale_y_log10(limits = c(NA, NA)) +
    labs(y = paste(gsub("\\.", " ", boxplot_variable), "(Log10)"))
}

bp
```
